text:
Luke Schenn's career is a map of the league: Toronto, Philadelphia, Los Angeles, Arizona, Anaheim, Tampa Bay (two Stanley Cups), Nashville, Winnipeg, a deadline stop in Buffalo last March, and now his third stint in Vancouver after signing as a free agent this summer. He is 37 and past 1,120 games.

His role is the one he has played for a decade: hit (36 in 12 games), block shots (16) and kill penalties. The numbers say the five-on-five minutes are rough. With him on the ice the Canucks have taken just 33.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with his teams creating almost nothing offensively when he played.

The context is a hard Vancouver start, with nine straight losses in the games he has dressed for. His ice time has dipped to around 12 minutes over the last ten. We'd watch whether the Canucks keep him in the lineup as a steadying presence or turn the spot over to younger legs.
headline: Luke Schenn, 37, back in Vancouver for a third time
